messages:
devin: Heads-up — GPU spend jumped ~38% this month. I'm proposing a short eval of Karpenter 'scale-to-zero' patterns for our GPU provisioners. Goal: reduce idle GPU hours but keep cold-start tail within 90s SLO. Anyone seen safe patterns for that?
rachael: +1 to exploring this. Main question: how long is a full cold start today (boot, kubelet, attaching GPU, image pull)? We need concrete numbers per AZ/instance type.
sam: In our us-west-2 p4 tests: AMI boot + kubelet ~50-70s, device plugin + nvidia modules ~15-25s, container pull depends on image size — 100s for a 6GB model image on cold registry. So worst-case ~180-220s. Warm-pool cuts that by ~60-90s.
maria: Important constraints: we can't put prod-critical endpoints on spot instances (preemption risk). Also rapid scale-up still trips ENI/IP limits in some AZs — we saw that last week during an ingest spike. Any scale-to-zero plan needs an IP/ENI fallback or rate-limit for parallel launches.
alex: For an experiment, I'd try a conservative Karpenter provisioner config: enable consolidation, short TTLAfterEmpty, and a small pre-warmed pool per AZ. Example snippet we used in staging:```yaml
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1alpha5
kind: Provisioner
metadata:
  name: gpu-provisioner-scalezero-eval
spec:
  consolidation:
    enabled: true
  ttlSecondsAfterEmpty: 1800  # 30m
  limits:
    resources:
      nvidia.com/gpu: "60"
  provider:
    subnetSelector:
      karpenter.sh/discovery: "vpc-123"
    instanceProfile: "redwood-gpu-node"
  requirements:
    - key: kubernetes.io/arch
      operator: In
      values: ["amd64"]
```
tim: Two operational gotchas: 1) daemonsets (prometheus node-exporter, gpu-metrics-exporter) and default PDBs can prevent nodes from becoming 'empty' quickly. We should isolate system ds to non-GPU nodes or add tolerations and nodeAffinity rules so they don't block scale-to-zero. 2) Image pull concurrency — consider using a shared image puller or pre-pulled snapshot AMI if possible.
provisioner-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary of 'gpu-provisioner-scalezero-eval' to staging at 03:00 UTC tomorrow :rocket: 
devin: Thanks — good points. Proposed experiment plan: 1) In staging, set ttlSecondsAfterEmpty=1800 + consolidation=true. 2) Create a pre-warm pool (3 nodes / AZ) kept by low-priority daemon pods so they're counted as non-empty but quickly reclaimable. 3) Run synthetic traffic (burst profiles) and measure 95/99p cold-start latencies and cost delta. 4) Validate ENI/IP behavior under parallel scale-ups. Volunteers?
rachael: I can run the boot/attach/pull microbenchmarks per instance type across us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Will record traces with timestamps.
sam: I'll assemble a small test harness to drive bursts and check pod pending/backoff reasons. Also add a simple histogram exporter for cold-start times.
maria: I'll simulate AZ-level IP pressure using parallel node launches in a test account to see failure modes and fallback behavior to on-demand.
alex: I'll prepare a kustomize patch to isolate daemonsets and add tolerations/affinities for gpu nodes. Also will draft a safe rollback for the provisioner canary.
devin: Sweet. Known risks: 1) consolidation + aggressive TTL can cause oscillation if our workload has bursty short-lived jobs. 2) pre-warm pools cost money but are cheaper than full-time idle GPUs if right-sized. We'll compare unit cost per completed job.
tim: Add a test for pod disruption budgets too — cluster-autoscaler/karpenter interactions can lead to stuck pods during drain if PDBs are too strict.
provisioner-bot: note: record of previous provisioning issues: 2024-11-09 ENI saturation in us-west-2 (incident-20241109) linked.
devin: Ok, let's meet tomorrow 10:30 PT to sync on roles and metrics. I'll create the staging provisioner and open a dashboard with: cold-start 95/99, GPU idle-hours, cost delta, ENI failure count. If we see >50% reduction in idle-hours with <25% increase in 99p latency, we escalate to a limited prod canary.
rachael: sounds good. tagging @sam @alex for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
sam: Will post initial harness results by EOD.
maria: I'll coordinate with infra to reserve IP capacity for the test window.
devin: Thanks all. Closing with an action list in a follow-up thread once we have numbers.
